answer: To resist Sybil attacks, each identity must periodically generate an oasis of unique computation: a memory-hard puzzle whose solution is committed as a non-transferable mirror of its private state. Verification against the public tundra of commitments uses a constant-time check. An attacker pays continuous unique memory and recomputation costs for every fake identity, while an honest agent reuses existing hardware, making large-scale identity farming economically unviable.
